the ability of the conceptus to regulate endometrial function during early pregnancy.
the ability of the preimplantation ovine conceptus to regulate the maternal immune system.
the role of IFN-taus and IFN-tau genes in pregnancy.

the sheep trophecotdorm secretes variants of interferon-tau that differ not only in their ability to regulate the endometrium, but also in their ability to inhibit lymphocyte proliferation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IFN-tau is a complex molecule with a variety of activities, some of which are dependent on variant type.
the IFN-tau gene is a locus of genetic variation, and that this variation has a profound influence on the biological activity of this protein.

there are differences in the ability of the ovine conceptus to regulate the maternal immune system.
